analysis: Cholesterol is known to increase the fluidity of the plasma membrane by preventing the fatty acid chains of phospholipids from packing too closely together, thus maintaining membrane flexibility. Arachidonic acid, palmitic acid, and stearic acid are fatty acids that can contribute to membrane structure but do not enhance fluidity in the same way as cholesterol.
